findings.title: Store boot validates the same objects repeatedly
findings.status: existing efficiency-review finding; not a new proposal
evidence: aienux@18e276590424593647cd7c39c6d16c2f9f8d6027 native/kernel/svc/store_boot.c:269-274 calls unkeyed st_open then ss_open; recovery keyslot path calls ss_keyslot_bootstrap at :485
2026-10-21 efficiency review G4-os-1: store_engine.c validates both slots by reading/hashing objects; sealed verification and keyslot bootstrap add more passes
findings.opportunity: Reuse a single validated immutable-object digest/result across slot comparison and sealed-record checks where the trust boundary permits. Keep separate authentication and structural validation semantics; do not accept a cached result across changed bytes or an untrusted generation.
findings.exactness: Potentially exact if reuse is keyed to the validated content/object identity and validity scope; no implementation equivalence established here.
findings.owner: No owner listed in prior review; route via coordinator before any patch.
findings.cheapest_discriminator: Instrument dev_read count and SHA-256 input bytes in the QEMU store gate on the same populated image; compare current path with a read-only in-memory validation-result cache. Measure mount latency separately; all timings UNKNOWN.
findings.quantitative_status: Prior review's 5x ordinary / 7x keyslot-path reduction is a structural pass-count derivation, not a measured boot speedup.

findings.title: Store serializes extent I/O as synchronous 4 KiB unit calls
findings.status: existing efficiency-review finding; driver improvement exists on a non-main branch
evidence: aienux@18e276590424593647cd7c39c6d16c2f9f8d6027 native/store/store_engine.c:71-105 reads one unit per dev_read; :330-343 writes one unit per dev_write
prior review G4-os-2 says driver queue depth 32/direct DMA is in L199 branch, while Store caller still issues one synchronous unit per call
findings.opportunity: Add extent/batched transfer at the Store boundary and preserve per-object hash, zero-padding, error ordering, and crash semantics. The disk queue-depth driver alone cannot help if this layer submits one command then waits.
findings.exactness: Exact data/result semantics are possible; request ordering and partial-I/O failure behavior must be preserved and tested.
findings.owner: L199 owns the NVMe driver; Store-layer change had no owner in G4-os-2. Coordinator should assign only after checking present ownership.
findings.cheapest_discriminator: On a copied QEMU Store image, count commands for a multi-unit extent and replay identical read/write/crash tests. Prior L199 branch reported 1,021.5 vs 7,877.4 MB/s at QD1/QD31 in QEMU; that is not Spark SSD evidence and not the Store-layer gain.
findings.quantitative_status: Prior 7.71x ratio is driver QEMU read-throughput data, not a measured Store speedup; Spark result UNKNOWN.

findings.title: X25519's 16x16 limb multiply is much wider than the existing 5-limb field implementation
findings.status: existing efficiency-review finding; source path confirmed at canonical main pin
evidence: aienux@18e276590424593647cd7c39c6d16c2f9f8d6027 native/net/x25519.c:42-54 performs 16x16 limb products and uses multiplication for squaring
prior review G4-os-6 locates Ed25519's five-limb field implementation at native/sig/ed25519.c:22,74-97
findings.opportunity: Consider a shared audited field representation or a dedicated five-limb X25519 implementation, reusing before rebuilding. Same prime supports the algebraic transformation; representation, reduction, constant-time behavior, and RFC 7748 edge cases still need proof.
findings.exactness: Exact modular arithmetic is required; this is not an approximation. A count of 256 vs 25 limb products (10.24x) does not imply that speed ratio.
findings.owner: No owner listed in G4-os-6; coordinator must reconcile current crypto owners first.
findings.cheapest_discriminator: Host differential against the existing implementation over RFC 7748 vectors plus boundary/random inputs, then native handshake timing on Spark; report timing only with a receipt.
findings.quantitative_status: 10.24x fewer inner products is operation-count arithmetic from the prior review. End-to-end handshake speedup UNMEASURED.

findings.title: Ed25519 verification performs two independent scalar-multiplication loops
findings.status: existing efficiency-review finding; implementation not verified here
evidence: aienux@18e276590424593647cd7c39c6d16c2f9f8d6027 native/sig/ed25519.c:248-263 defines a fixed 256-step scalar multiplication; :545-548 invokes it for [S]B and [k]A
findings.opportunity: Use a public-input joint double-scalar multiplication (shared doubling loop) for verification, retaining the existing path as a differential oracle and keeping signing constant-time. Signature verification result must remain exact.
findings.exactness: Exact group result, not lossy; signature verification uses public signature/key inputs. Keep canonical encoding and rejection checks unchanged.
findings.owner: No owner listed in G4-os-7; check current ownership before assigning.
findings.cheapest_discriminator: Run RFC 8032 valid/invalid vectors and differential randomized signatures on host; then time verify-only batch on Spark with identical inputs.
findings.quantitative_status: Prior 2.29x count of group operations is an algebraic estimate; wall-clock gain UNKNOWN.

findings.title: Search already has equivalence pruning; AIEN_0 should learn ordering over equivalence classes, not rediscover duplicate states
findings.status: existing mechanism; promising measurement gap, avoid duplicate implementation
evidence: omega-mv canonical main pin from git ls-remote: a8ffd2b912c84197d08f963b05f9c7d8b30a3f8a
available Omega source copy reports src/crumbline/cl_search.c:249,290 hashes states and :265 applies candidate cutoff; source copy is an older worktree, not treated as canonical-main proof
prior L303 brief identifies src/searchtrace and spec/searchtrace/M23_SEARCH_TRACE_CORPUS_V1.md as built trace-corpus code; trace format records ST_PRUNE_EQUIV and a dedup task setting
findings.opportunity: Treat each exact-equivalence class as one search state and train/rank its representatives. Reuse the existing hash/equivalence and M23 trace corpus. First quantify duplicate-prune share and solved-at-equal-verification-budget by task; do not build a second hash-cons/e-graph layer unless current code shows an uncovered equivalence relation.
findings.exactness: Equivalence pruning must be exact for the declared observations. Learned score/order is approximate and may change which candidates fit a finite budget; the verifier remains authoritative and outside the model.
findings.owner: L303 owns AIEN_0/M23 training integration; L049 is the plan-reuse campaign. Parent/coordinator routes follow-on, no duplicate worker.
findings.cheapest_discriminator: Replay frozen task set with equivalence dedup on/off and current order, count exact equivalence-pruned candidates, verifier calls, solved tasks and first-solution cost. No model load or timing needed for initial counts.
findings.quantitative_status: Corpus/task counts and benefit UNKNOWN in this audit; no corpus gate or benchmark run.

findings.title: AIEN_0 is a small synthesis-policy ranker, but no canonical implementation/evaluation was present
findings.status: active existing L303 objective; not a new training proposal; completion not demonstrated
evidence: aien-train canonical main ed8b6ea2562efdda7913234ca8f34b443714a987: README.md:3-7 says pre-alpha, Omega/no-CUDA path, claims must link source or receipt; docs/PLAN.md:12 prohibits third-party training framework in product path

aien0/m20 remote ref resolves to the same ed8b6ea2562efdda7913234ca8f34b443714a987; expected Spark worktree ~/workspace/aien-train-aien0 was absent; no AIEN_0 artifact/status was found in canonical tracked main
L303 brief: rank next Omega operation from synthesis traces; oracle training then M21/M22 path; held-out equal-verification-budget search test; model size guided by L279
findings.opportunity: Prioritize a compact candidate scorer that ranks operations/states using only decision-time features. Evaluate imitation, pairwise ranking and value heads on the same frozen tasks, then compare learned order against current/random/cheapest-first at equal verifier budget. This is search-control efficiency, not a replacement verifier.
findings.exactness: The learned policy is approximate and can miss solutions under finite budget. Correctness stays exact only because Omega's verifier decides acceptance; report solve-rate/regret separately from semantic correctness.
findings.owner: L303; no duplicate implementation or worker. Coordinate status recovery with parent and do not close ledger.
findings.cheapest_discriminator: Read-only first: recover the already-assigned worktree/handoff and inspect source/status. Then perform non-timed held-out task counts for existing order vs random vs cheapest-first vs scorer at one fixed verifier-call budget. Do not load a model or run hardware measurements for this audit.
findings.quantitative_status: No AIEN_0 trained weights, train receipt, held-out advantage, or energy result verified. UNKNOWN, not a negative result.

findings.title: Training-state compression is a separate lossy tradeoff; optimizer-pass reuse is the exact first lever
findings.status: existing L304 design notes from prior review; AIEN_0 applicability unproven
evidence: aien-train@ed8b6ea2562efdda7913234ca8f34b443714a987 README.md:5 frames weight-residency as a thesis under test; repo is pre-alpha and has no training code in canonical main
prior efficiency review G5-physics-train-6/7 and ledger L304 describe 28 B/parameter/step for one illustrative fused AdamW layout, plus a 1.4x byte reduction using BF16 m/v states
findings.opportunity: For any implemented trainer, first accumulate microbatches and execute one fused optimizer update per chosen token batch; avoid repeating the same state read/write per microbatch. Evaluate BF16 optimizer state only as a separately labelled lossy experiment after exact FP32 baseline exists.
findings.exactness: Optimizer-update frequency changes training trajectory; low-precision m/v is lossy. Neither is algebraically identical to full-precision per-microbatch updates. Do not transfer LLM-scale crossover numbers to AIEN_0 without its parameter count, batch, shapes and measured bandwidth.
findings.owner: L304 owns training target; L279 physics and L294 kernel backlog. Use their existing owners/receipts, do not open duplicate work.
findings.cheapest_discriminator: Once an AIEN_0 training executable exists, compare exact same-seed short runs for fused vs reference FP32 updates, check parameter/optimizer-state equality, then measure bytes and elapsed time. Only after this control, compare BF16-state held-out ranking quality.
findings.quantitative_status: Prior 626-token crossover and 2.07x example are derived from an illustrative optimizer layout and external ceiling inputs, not measured or transferable to AIEN_0. AIEN_0 gains UNKNOWN.
